posts.text: 10 AI crawlers, and what each is for. Block the wrong one and you vanish from the answer. Block none and you train the models for free. Save this before you touch your robots.txt again.

posts.text:
Your robots.txt is talking to AI crawlers you've never heard of.

Block the wrong one and you vanish from the answer. Block none and you train the models for free.

The 10 that matter, and what each one actually does:
alt: Reference table titled '10 AI crawlers, and what each is for', 10 of the 19 we allow. OpenAI: GPTBot trains the model (yes), OAI-SearchBot builds the search index (always), ChatGPT-User fetches live mid-answer (yes). Anthropic: ClaudeBot trains the model (yes), Claude-SearchBot indexes for citation (always), Claude-User fetches on request (yes). Google-Extended: Gemini training, not Search (yes). PerplexityBot indexes for citation (always). Applebot-Extended: Apple Intelligence (yes). CCBot: feeds almost everyone (yes). Never block OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot or PerplexityBot. One robots.txt rule is enough to vanish from one assistant. Most AI crawlers never run JavaScript, so ship real HTML.

posts.title: The schema types that actually get you cited

posts.text: There are 800+ schema types. Eight of them matter. Save this one.
alt: Blue poster: '800 schema types. Eight matter.' The eight an AI reads to decide who you are.
Organization and Person: the two schema types that say you exist.
Article and FAQPage: the two schema types that make you quotable.
BreadcrumbList and WebPage: the two schema types that give a page an address.
Product if it has a price, LocalBusiness if it has an address: the last two schema types.
Blue poster: 'The other 792 are noise.' Start with Organization and FAQPage.

posts.text:
Schema.org has 800+ types.

Eight of them decide whether AI can cite you. The other 792 are noise.

Here's the eight, and what each one is actually for:
alt: Blue poster headline: '800 schema types. Eight matter.' Underneath: 'The eight types an AI reads before it decides who you are.' Save this one.

Who you are: 'Two types say you exist.' 01 Organization, one per site: the entity every other type points back to; your name, your logo, one place a machine can read. 02 Person, named humans: sameAs links out, so the name resolves to someone real.

Where things sit: 'Give the page an address.' 05 BreadcrumbList, the path in: where the page sits among the rest, and the route a crawler takes to reach it. 06 WebPage, one per page: what the page is, under an @id that stays put while the page keeps changing.
Blue poster headline: 'The other 792 are noise.' Start with Organization and FAQPage; the rest can wait a week. Link: runaudit.devmarde.com. Ali Mehdi, builds it, then markets it.
